The '''LX-80''' was an anti-[[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]] emplacement. Developed by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]], the launcher used [[Missile/Legends|missiles]] designed for the company's [[PLX series]] of portable missile launchers. The LX-80 launcher contained eighty missiles in as many missile tubes, and an automatic loader could reload those tubes with the launcher's reserve of missiles when the first payload was expended.

==Description==
The LX-80 was a [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]] developed by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] for installation at bases and other facilities. The emplacement filled an anti-[[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] role and utilized [[Missile/Legends|missiles]] originally designed for Merr-Sonn's [[PLX series]] of portable missile launchers, ordnance that was readily available from [[Arms dealer/Legends|arms dealers]]. These missiles were stored in a rack of missile tubes stacked four high and twenty wide, providing a supply of eighty missiles. An automatic loader could load the LX-80's reserve of eighty additional missiles if all of the tubes were empty, though a misfire in even one tube could prevent the weapon from being reloaded until the blockage was cleared.<ref name="H&S" />

As was the case with the PLX series, "dumb" rockets, "smart" GAM rockets, and "savant" rockets could be used in the LX-80. "Dumb" rockets had no guidance system, flying in a given direction until either contacting the target or expending their [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]].<ref name="H&S" /> "Smart" missiles were of the [[Gravity-Activated Mode guided missile]] type developed specifically for the PLX series, which could follow either [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]] signatures in EPR mode or [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]-wave anomalies created by [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] in GAM mode.<ref name="ISB">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref> "Savant" missiles fired like "dumb" missiles, allowing targeted [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] to believe that they had evaded them. However, after flying for a short [[Time/Legends|time]], the savant missile would activate its targeting systems and establish a lock, homing in on its target. These missiles had a range of approximately ten [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] when fired from the LX-80,<ref name="H&S" /> though GAM missiles could pursue their targets for up to forty kilometers.<ref name="ISB" />

==History==
The LX-80 launcher retailed for 75,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="H&S" />

==Behind the scenes==
The LX-80 has so far only been referenced in ''[[Hideouts & Strongholds]]'', a [[1998]] supplement for use with the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] book [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]. The book's introduction states that the bases in the book are intended to be generic, and that the book's material could be worked into a roleplaying campaign set at any point between the [[Old Republic era|time]] of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series and the [[New Republic era]]. This ambiguity means that the timeframe of the LX-80's [[in-universe]] usage cannot be precisely dated, though its intentional interoperability with ordnance for the PLX-series<ref name="H&S" /> suggests an introduction at some point after the debut of the [[PLX-1/Legends|PLX-1 portable missile launcher]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Databank">{{DB|technology|plex|portable missile launcher}}</ref>

The book refers to the launcher's manufacturer as "MerrSonn" instead of the much more common "Merr-Sonn." This article therefore reflects the more widespread usage of the latter.
